item.title: MAC Minute — 2026-10-02
item.description:
MAC Fellas, Saturday morning. We are looking at three major shifts in global air cargo capacity and demand. First, Ethiopian Airlines is investing five billion dollars in a new cargo fleet and the Bishoftu hub. That is a massive infrastructure play. It could significantly reshape competition across African trade lanes. Meanwhile, Flydubai Cargo just launched its first dedicated freighter network with three B737-800s. They are targeting e-commerce and specialized shipments that narrowbody belly capacity cannot handle efficiently. Finally, Xeneta reports shippers are demanding short-term deals because demand is squeezing available capacity. That volatility suggests booking strategies may need to become more flexible in the coming weeks. Watch how these new entrants and shifting contract behaviors impact regional rates this quarter.
